messages:
Maya: Morning handoff — quick run: I’m out at 11:30 PT for a demo. Leaving coverage to @Sam and @Jordan.
Maya: What changed: deployed canary for /generate V2 at 09:20, routing 10% to v2 (no errors observed). Cache warmers kicked off for high-volume prefixes.
Maya: Watch: small uptick in latencies on eu-west at sequence lengths >1024 (p95 ~ 340ms -> 480ms). Likely due to kernel selection path falling back.
Sam: noted. Any logs or query samples to check?
Maya: yes — I left a short grep script in #eng-sre playbook, and added a dashboard link: https://console.redwood/observability/dashboards/hand-off/3860
Maya: Quick command if you need to repro tailing the canary:
Maya: ```kubectl logs -f deployment/generator-canary -c runtime --since=10m | grep "seq_len"```
Jordan: I’ll keep an eye on eu-west p95 and bump canary down if we see errors. What’s the rollback plan?
Maya: Rollback is straightforward — change traffic to 0% via rollout API: POST /rollouts/canary/adjust body {"percent":0} or use console quick action. I added the runbook note under /runbooks/canary-rollback.
Ari: FYI — there’s a scheduled maintenance for dedicated-gpu-pool-3 at 02:00 UTC (tomorrow). It may briefly reduce capacity for some Dedicated tenants. Notification sent to affected customers.
oncall-bot: Reminder: scheduled job "kv-evict-check" runs at 02:15 UTC, will log eviction spikes to /var/log/evictions.log.
Sam: Thanks — I’ll make sure autoscaler policy for the pooling namespace is set to allow burst +1 node in case of small capacity drop.
Jordan: Small ask — there’s a flaky CR I left in review (PR #922) that changes batching strategy. If someone can merge before the end of the day that would help reduce load on the fallback kernel.
Maya: I skimmed it, left one comment about adding a unit test for the batching window. @Ari can you take a quick look before 11?
Ari: I can review now. Point me to the test gaps.
Maya: Thanks — the missing test covers concurrent requests when batch timeout fires. Example snippet I pasted in the PR.
Sam: Action items for on-call: 1) Monitor eu-west p95 for sequence_len>1024 (dashboard link in first msg). 2) If p95 > 600ms or error rate >0.5% for 5m, scale canary down to 0% and page eng-sre. 3) Watch dedicated-gpu-pool-3 capacity during maintenance window.
Jordan: I’ll own item 1 and 2 while you’re out, Sam will monitor item 3.
Maya: Appreciate it. One more: there’s a demo traffic spike expected at 10:45 PT (internal). Try to avoid large config changes around that time.
Ari: Got it — blocking non-critical deploys 10:30-11:00 PT.
Sam: Quick question — do we want to pre-warm KV cache prefixes for the demo?
Maya: Yes — I triggered the prewarm job, but it may need a manual kick for some low-hit prefixes: `python tools/prewarm.py --prefix demo-2026-03 -t 30s`
Sam: I’ll run it in a minute.
Jordan: FYI I’m putting a short note in the rota doc so afternoon oncall knows to follow up on the canary metrics.
Maya: Last note: I added a regression check set to the optimizer that will auto-signal if cost/token increases more than 7% versus baseline for the last 1h. If that fires, it’s likely due to a quantization change — check model variant routing.
Sam: Roger. Anything else?
Maya: No — handing off now. Thanks all, ping if you need me before 11:30. :wave:
Sam: :thumbsup: Good luck with the demo.
Jordan: :eyes: I’ll message if the p95 climbs.
Ari: Reviewing PR #922 now.
oncall-bot: Deployment event recorded: canary rollout 3860021980 -> 3860022020, 10% -> 10% (no change).
